sentence: This project tests whether an artificial intelligence screening strategy can detect narrowing of the aortic valve in older adults before symptoms begin.
This project studies how neutrophils and neutrophil extracellular traps promote cancer in mouse models of cancer predisposition.
This project builds an adaptor-directed system that helps T cells target solid cancers precisely, and uses imaging to improve it.
This project uses biology, computer science and engineering to predict where to intervene in complex gene networks in diseases like cancer.
This project studies how a compact RNA-guided enzyme works, to make it a better genome-editing tool.
This project builds a tool that uses computer vision and sensing technology to measure how visually accessible indoor spaces are for people with vision impairment.
This project tests whether viral proteins made by HIV damage the blood vessels of the lungs, using animal models, human specimens and cultured cells.
This project studies how Prevotella in the airway causes subclinical inflammation and interferes with Streptococcus pneumoniae sticking to epithelial cells.
This project tests whether T cells reprogrammed in the blood to display a chimeric antigen receptor can fight ovarian cancer in mouse models.
This project studies how cholinergic neurons in the basal forebrain and their pathways to the amygdala control feeding and body weight.
This project studies how drugs act in people and why individuals respond differently, using omics science, artificial intelligence and machine learning.
This project studies how cells use small metabolites in normal skin wounds and how this changes in diabetic wounds, causing delayed healing.
This project refines a two-step test that measures matrix metalloproteinase activity in osteosarcoma extracellular vesicles to track how patients respond to treatment.
This project compares how sitting, arm movement and babbling develop in infants with Down syndrome who do or do not have congenital heart defects.
This project uses DNA and tissue samples from people with genetic hearing loss, and mice, to develop gene therapy methods for hearing loss.
This project studies how two drugs used against HIV are activated and deactivated in the colon.
This project builds an assay that detects changes in DNA fragmentation patterns in blood to predict aggressive forms of prostate cancer.
This project studies how phosphodiesterases regulate signaling and arrhythmia in heart failure, and how this differs between men and women.
This project sets up a center to model how genetic variation in noncoding regions of DNA contributes to many diseases.
